_comment: What the stub judge answers. Layer it in front of the stage replies:
A judge is asked a different question, in dossier's own wrapper (R7.19):
the rubric, the document in full, the candidate inside <claim>...</claim>, and
'Answer with JSON only'. Each rule below matches on that opening tag plus the
first words of one candidate -- anchored there on purpose. A rule matching a
phrase from the candidate alone would also match every other candidate about
the same document, because the wrapper puts the whole document in the prompt:
the stub would answer 'supported' to a planted claim and measure 90% instead
of 100%, and the number would look like a judge being careful.
Only `supported` is asserted by any rule (R7.12). `evidence` is for the person
reading a disagreement back before signing off a threshold.
This stub agrees with all twenty human verdicts on purpose, so the exercise
measures 100%. Flip one `supported` to see 95%, and to see why a bar at 1.0
would be one nobody can hold.

match: <claim>The gateway upgrade shipped a connection pool whose idle timeout was 3

reply.evidence: The root cause section states exactly this.

match: <claim>A mismatch between the connection pool's idle timeout and the load bal

reply.evidence: The same cause in the reviewer's own words; the note gives both timeouts.

match: <claim>Requests handed an already-closed socket waited for the full client ti

reply.evidence: Stated in the root cause section.

match: <claim>The payment gateway vendor had an outage during the window.

reply.evidence: The note names the upgrade shipped the previous evening as the only change; it says nothing about a vendor outage.

match: <claim>Checkout was overwhelmed by traffic after the upgrade was announced.

reply.evidence: No traffic figure appears anywhere in the note.

match: <claim>The export job was scheduled at a fixed time rather than triggered by

reply.evidence: The root cause section states exactly this.

reply.evidence: The root cause section says the window was one it had no way of knowing about.

match: <claim>An upstream warehouse load that finished late pushed the export past t

reply.evidence: The timeline states the late load and the 05:30 UTC window.

match: <claim>The warehouse load failed, so the export had nothing to read.

reply.evidence: The load finished late; the note never says it failed.

match: <claim>A caching bug in the dashboard showed the previous day's figures.

reply.evidence: The dashboard was stale because the export had not finished, not because of a caching bug.

match: <claim>A firewall change written against a stale network inventory replaced t

reply.evidence: The root cause section states exactly this.

reply.evidence: Stated in the root cause section.

reply.evidence: The timeline and the root cause section both state this.

reply.evidence: Nothing in the note mentions certificates.

reply.evidence: Authentication requests were dropped at the firewall; no identity provider is mentioned.

reply.evidence: The root cause section states exactly this.

reply.evidence: Stated in the timeline and the root cause section.

reply.evidence: Both halves are stated: the traffic in the timeline, the rebuild in the root cause.

reply.evidence: The notes section says the opposite: traffic was within the planned capacity.

match: <claim>The autoscaler was misconfigured and added pods too slowly.

reply.evidence: The notes section says the autoscaler reacted as configured.
